name: Modules.Geofence
summary: Provides a battery-efficient way to monitor a device's movement into or out of a geographic region.
description:
This feature requires a Pro or Enterprise subscription!

You use the Geofence module to define and monitor geofences in your application. A geofence is a circular region defined by a point (a latitude/longitude pair) and a radius, and represented by the [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object. When a device moves into or out of a geofence being monitored, the module notifies your application of the event. Enterprise customers can also define geofences on the server using the Appcelerator Cloud Services API. An application can query the server for any defined geofences and begin monitoring them. See the RegionMonitoring example in the module ZIP download. ## Getting Started Once you have [installed](#!/guide/Using_a_Module) the module, use `require()` to access it from JavaScript: ``` javascript var Geofence = require('ti.geofence'); ``` ### Location Permissions Please ensure to request proper location permissions before attempting to use geofencing feautures. See [Titanium.Geolocation.hasLocationPermissions(type)](api:Titanium.Geolocation#hasLocationPermissions) and [Titanium.Geolocation.requestLocationPermissions(type, callback)](api:Titanium.Geolocation#requestLocationPermissions) for details. Example: ``` javascript if (!Ti.Geolocation.hasLocationPermissions(Ti.Geolocation.AUTHORIZATION_ALWAYS)) { Ti.Geolocation.requestLocationPermissions(Ti.Geolocation.AUTHORIZATION_ALWAYS, function (e) { if (!e.success) { alert('Location permissions declined!'); return; } alert('Location permissions ready'); // Initialize monitoring here }); } ``` ### Creating and monitoring geofence regions You use the [Geofence.createRegion()](api:Modules.Geofence#createRegion) method to define a [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object. A geofence is a circular area defined by a point (latitude and longitude) and a radius (in meters). ``` javascript var newRegion = Geofence.createRegion({ center: { latitude: 37.389601, longitude: -122.050169 }, radius: 500, identifier: 'Appcelerator' }); ``` To start monitoring a region, call the [Geofence.startMonitoringForRegions()](api:Modules.Geofence#startMonitoringForRegions) method, passing it the region or regions you want to monitor. ``` javascript Geofence.startMonitoringForRegions([region1, region2]); ``` To be notified when the device moves into or out of a geofence region, create an event listener for the [enterregions](api:Modules.Geofence#enterregions) or [exitregions](api:Modules.Geofence#exitregions) events, respectively. For example: ``` javascript Geofence.addEventListener('enterregions', function (e) { e.regions.forEach(function (region) { // Display local notification showNotification({ title: 'ENTER', body: 'enter - ' + region.identifier }); }); }); ``` The event object passed to the event handler contains a `regions` property that identifies the region(s) that were entered or exited. On iOS this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects; on Android, it contains an array of generic objects that each contain a property called `identifier`. The value of this property corresponds to the one assigned to the [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) when it was created. ## Testing Geofence monitoring You have a few options for testing geofence monitoring in your application. One approach is field testing: travel (drive, walk, etc.) between monitored regions while the application is running. You can also pass mock location data to the application running on a device or Simulator. Note: The timing and frequency of location events may vary from one environment to another (device, OS version, network availability). ### Mock locations from the iOS Simulator Once the application is running in the simulator, select **Debug** > **Location** in the Simulator and select a predefined location or route that you would like to be sent to the Simulator. You can also enter a custom location (latitude, longitude). ### Mock locations using Xcode This method will work on both the iOS Simulator and on device. 1. Launch your application once, then go to the build folder of your project and open the Xcode project found in **build/iphone/**. 2. Run your project using Xcode. 3. Once app is running, in Xcode debug area, click the Simulate Location icon to display a list of mock locations that can be sent to your application. 5. Select one of these locations to send it to your app. Alternately, click on **Add GPX File to Project...** and select a GPX file with mock locations. A GPX file is provided in the **example/MockLocationData** folder in module download. The route starts at North De Anza Blvd and I-280 in Cupertino, CA and travels north on I-280. 8. After adding a GPX file, go back and click on the mock locations arrow. The GPX file should now be in the list. Select the mock location to start using it. ### Mock locations on Android Add the following to your `tiapp.xml`. ``` xml ``` For more information, see [Provide Mock Location Data](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/location/strategies#MockData) ### Sample applications The module ZIP file contains two Geofence sample applications (**examples/Basic** and **examples/RegionMonitoring**) and a GPX file (**examples/MockLocationData**) for mocking location data in Xcode.

properties.name: LOCATION_STATUS_ERROR
properties.summary: Possible value of the `errorcode` property in the [error](api:Modules.Geofence#error) event object indicating an unspecified error occurred.

properties.name: LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE
properties.summary: Possible value of the `errorcode` property in the [error](api:Modules.Geofence#error) event object indicating the geofence service is not available now.

properties.name: LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_GEOFENCES
properties.summary: Possible value of the `errorcode` property in the [error](api:Modules.Geofence#error) event object indicating your application has registered more than 100 geofences.

properties.name: LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_PENDING_INTENTS
properties.summary: Possible value of the `errorcode` property in the [error](api:Modules.Geofence#error) event object.

properties.name: monitoredRegions
properties.summary: An array of the regions currently being monitored for the current application.

properties.name: REGION_STATE_INSIDE
properties.summary: Possible value of the `state` property in the [regionstate](api:Modules.Geofence#regionstate) event object.
properties.description: The location is inside the given region.

properties.name: REGION_STATE_OUTSIDE
properties.summary: Possible value of the `state` property in the [regionstate](api:Modules.Geofence#regionstate) event object.
properties.description: The location is outside of the given region.

properties.name: REGION_STATE_UNKNOWN
properties.summary: Possible value of the `state` property in the [regionstate](api:Modules.Geofence#regionstate) event object.
properties.description: It is unknown whether the location is inside or outside of the region.

methods.name: createRegion

parameters.name: object
parameters.summary: Object with properties of the [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object.

methods.name: isGooglePlayServicesAvailable
methods.summary: Returns a number value indicating the availability of Google Play Services which are required to monitor regions.

deprecated.notes: Use [Modules.PlayServices.isGooglePlayServicesAvailable](Modules.PlayServices.isGooglePlayServicesAvailable) in Titanium SDK 7.0.0 and later.

methods.name: regionMonitoringAvailable
methods.summary: Returns a boolean that indicates if region monitoring is supported on the current device.

methods.name: requestStateForRegion
methods.summary: Asynchronously retrieve the cached state of the specified region.
methods.description: The state is returned to the delegate via the `regionstate` event.

methods.name: startMonitoringForRegions
methods.summary: Starts monitoring the [Region(s)](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) passed as a parameter.

parameters.name: Region
parameters.summary: Either an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects or a single [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object.

methods.name: stopMonitoringAllRegions
methods.summary: Stops monitoring all of the regions that are currently being monitored.
methods.description:
This method is asynchronous on Android. The `removeregions` event will fire on completion.

Example:

``` javascript
Geofence.stopMonitoringAllRegions();
```

methods.name: stopMonitoringForRegions
methods.summary: Stops monitoring the specified region or regions.
methods.description:
Takes either an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects or a single
[Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object as an argument.

This method is asynchronous on Android. The `removeregions` event will fire on completion.

``` javascript
Geofence.stopMonitoringForRegions([region, region1]);
```

parameters.name: Region
parameters.summary: Either an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects or a single [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) object.

events.name: enterregions
events.summary: Fired when the device enters a monitored region.

properties.name: regions
properties.summary: The region(s) that were entered. On iOS, this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects representing the regions that were entered. On Android, this property contains an array of generic objects, each of which has an [identifier](api:Modules.Geofence.Region#identifier) property that corresponds to the region(s) that were entered.

events.name: error
events.summary: Fired when there is an error, or monitoring failed for a region.

properties.name: error
properties.summary: A string that describes the error.

properties.name: errorcode
properties.summary: A number that describes the error (Android, only). Can be one of the following: [LOCATION_STATUS_ERROR](api:Modules.Geofence#LOCATION_STATUS_ERROR), [LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE](api:Modules.Geofence#LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_NOT_AVAILABLE), [LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_GEOFENCES](api:Modules.Geofence#LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_GEOFENCES), [LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_PENDING_INTENTS](api:Modules.Geofence#LOCATION_STATUS_GEOFENCE_TOO_MANY_PENDING_INTENTS)

properties.name: regions
properties.summary: The regions for which monitoring failed. On iOS, this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects representing the regions for which monitoring failed. On Android, this property contains an array of generic objects, each of which has an [identifier](api:Modules.Geofence.Region#identifier) property that corresponds to the region(s) that were entered.

events.name: exitregions
events.summary: Fired when the device exits a monitored region.

properties.name: regions
properties.summary: The region(s) that were exited. On iOS, this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects representing the regions that were exited. On Android, this property contains an array of generic objects, each of which has an [identifier](api:Modules.Geofence.Region#identifier) property that corresponds to the region(s) that were exited.

events.name: monitorregions
events.summary: Fired when [startMonitoringForRegions()](api:Modules.Geofence#startMonitoringForRegions) and monitoring has successfully started for those regions.

properties.name: regions
properties.summary: The region(s) for which monitoring has started. On iOS, this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects representing the regions for which monitoring has started. On Android, there is no property for you to check.

events.name: regionstate
events.summary:
Fired when [requestStateForRegion()](api:Modules.Geofence#requestStateForRegion) requested a state or there is
a state transition for a monitored region.

properties.name: region
properties.summary: The region that triggered the state change.

properties.name: state
properties.summary: The updated region state. One of `REGION_STATE_*`.

events.name: removeregions
events.summary: Fired on Android when regions are removed using `stopMonitoringForRegions` or `stopMonitoringAllRegions` and monitoring has successfully stopped for those regions.

properties.name: regions
properties.summary: The region(s) for which monitoring has stopped. On iOS, this property contains an array of [Region](api:Modules.Geofence.Region) objects representing the regions for which monitoring has stopped. On Android, this property contains an array of generic objects, each of which has an [identifier](api:Modules.Geofence.Region#identifier) property that corresponds to the region(s) for which monitoring has stopped.
